oligo_notes: 13-mer lipid-conjugated N3'-P5' thiophosphoramidate telomerase template antagonist;NOT a PS-ASO;thrombocytopenia is on-target myelosuppression;CHEMISTRY IS NOT PHOSPHOROTHIOATE. Review states verbatim (printed p39): 'Imetelstat sodium is a sodium salt of a 13-mer oligonucleotide N3'-->P5' thio-phosphoramidate conjugated with a lipid palmitoyl group attached to the 5' terminus through an aminoglycerol linker. The structure of imetelstat sodium includes thiophosphoramidate linkages, with sulfurizaton of the native phosphodiester, and replacement of the 3'-oxygen to provide a 3'-amino group.' Clin Pharm exec summary (printed p76) repeats: '13-mer N3'->P5' thio-phosphoramidate oligonucleotide with a palmitoyl lipid covalently attached by an aminoglycerol linker to the 5' thio-phosphate of the first nucleotide'. ps_count recorded as 0 because every internucleoside linkage is explicitly an N3'->P5' THIOPHOSPHORAMIDATE (sulfur present, but 3'-N not 3'-O; chemically distinct from a phosphorothioate diester linkage) - i.e. the molecule carries 12 sulfurised NP-S linkages plus a 5' thio-phosphate but ZERO phosphorothioate linkages. backbone_chemistry forced to 'mixed' only because the schema enum has no thio-phosphoramidate term; the true value is 'full_NPS (N3'->P5' thiophosphoramidate)'. MECHANISM CAVEAT: imetelstat thrombocytopenia is telomerase-inhibitor myelosuppression acting on megakaryocyte progenitors (CFU-MK), NOT the phosphorothioate-backbone platelet-binding/aggregation mechanism that drives the ASO class signal - the review itself attributes the toxicity to on-target telomerase inhibition in normal haematopoietic progenitors (printed p46-47) while separately noting that imetelstat's complement activation and aPTT prolongation 'reflect the well-characterized toxicity profile of the related phosphorothioate ODN class' (printed p55). Treat this compound as a mechanistic OUT-GROUP for PS-content modelling. NO NUCLEOTIDE SEQUENCE IS PRINTED ANYWHERE IN THIS 442-PAGE DOCUMENT (regex search for [ACGTU]{8,25} returned zero hits; the structural formula/molecular formula section is a bitmap/redacted) - sequence_5to3 therefore stays TBD, not recalled from memory. Mechanism: covalently-lipidated 13-mer that binds the template region of hTR, competitively inhibiting hTERT (printed p22, p76). Approved (regular approval), NDA 217779, review completion 24 May 2024. Human exposure anchor used for in-vitro grading: popPK-predicted Cmax 89.2 ug/mL at 7.1 mg/kg q4w, fraction unbound 0.06 (free Cmax ~5.35 ug/mL) - printed p48.
effect_vs_control: no effect on clonogenicity of normal MK progenitors, while malignant CFU-MK from essential thrombocythemia patients were dose-dependently suppressed
source_table: Applicant Figure 1 'Differential Effects of Imetelstat on Megakaryocytes Growth' and accompanying Applicant's Position text (Baerlocher, 2019) (printed p44-45)
measurement_notes: CONTRADICTORY NEGATIVE ROW, kept deliberately. The Applicant states 'imetelstat selectively suppressed spontaneous growth of malignant CFU-MK from patients with ET in a dose-dependent manner, while having no effect on clonogenicity of normal MK progenitors' - graded 0 on that stated null result for NORMAL megakaryocyte progenitors. THIS DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS the Applicant's own Study GRN01 two pages later, in which normal human bone marrow CFU-MK were significantly inhibited at >=3.75 uM. The review does not reconcile the two. Any consumer should treat the normal-MK in-vitro picture as unresolved and weight GRN01 (a study the Applicant conducted, in normal marrow, with a stated concentration threshold) over the published ET-focused figure. readout_value and a numeric concentration are both TBD - Applicant Figure 1 is a bitmap dose-response plot with no printed values.

oligo_notes: Tricyclo-DNA (tcDNA) antisense oligonucleotide, fully modified, phosphorothioate backbone. The paper's main text does not print the oligonucleotide sequences (they are not in the Materials and Methods section retrieved from the Europe PMC full text), so sequence_5to3 is TBD rather than reconstructed. Well-tolerated benchmark tcDNA targeting the mouse Dmd exon 23; used as the non-toxic comparator throughout.
measurement_notes: Explicit no-effect result. For M23D: 'as opposed to the nontoxic M23D PS-tcDNA'. For H51(+67)W: 'nor activate human platelets, as shown in Figures 3C and 3D, where no changes in PAC1 or CD62P levels were detected with H51(+67)W'. Method: 50 uL human citrated platelet-rich plasma incubated with 2 mg/mL oligonucleotide (or 20 uM ADP as positive control) for 15 min at 37 C, then CD61/PAC1/CD62P flow cytometry. The paper states 2 mg/mL; recorded as 2000 ug/mL. Values are plotted in the figure only.

measurement_notes: HUMAN IN-VITRO ROW — the second-priority class for this dataset. WHY THIS ROW EXISTS AND THE THREE ON-TARGET ROWS DO NOT (the exclusion line, stated as instructed): pegnivacogin's reductions in ADP-induced CD62P (100% vs 89.79+/-4.04%, p=0.027, n=9), PAC-1 binding (100% vs 83.02+/-4.08%, p=0.010, n=11), LTA aggregation (97.71+/-5.30% vs 66.53+/-9.92%, p=0.013, n=10) and residual aggregation in RADAR patients after 1 mg/kg IV (100% vs 43.21+/-8.23%, p=0.020) are all DECREASES produced BY DESIGN — FIXa inhibition lowers thrombin generation, thrombin is 'a major platelet activator' (the paper's own Background), and the paper's Conclusion frames the result as 'a promising antithrombotic strategy'. That is intended anticoagulant pharmacology, is excluded per the anti-FIXa/anti-vWF rule, and is NOT entered as toxicity in any direction. THE ANIVAMERSEN CONDITION IS DIFFERENT AND IS IN SCOPE: with the aptamer's on-target activity neutralised by its complementary antidote, the oligonucleotides are still present in human whole blood, and the source reports NO platelet-activation signal — i.e. an explicit negative for a TARGET-INDEPENDENT (unintended) oligonucleotide-platelet interaction, which is precisely the hazard this dataset exists to capture for PS-ASOs and aptamers. GRADE 0 per the rubric's in-vitro column ('No activation, aggregation, or binding above vehicle control at tested concentration'). IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THE GRADE: the abstract phrases this as absence of ATTENUATION ('was not attenuated' / 'negated'), which asserts return to the control level rather than explicitly asserting 'no increase above control'; no increase is reported anywhere in the abstract, and no numbers are printed for this condition, so readout_value is TBD. If full text shows a supra-control CD62P rise under anivamersen this row becomes grade 1. readout_unit follows the abstract's own convention for these readouts (control normalised to 100%); the value itself was not printed. dose_or_conc_value is TBD, not the patients' 1 mg/kg bolus — the abstract gives no in-vitro pegnivacogin (or anivamersen) concentration, and importing the clinical dose would be an invented attribution. Full text inaccessible (paywalled) — see extraction_notes.

measurement_notes: HUMAN EX-VIVO PLATELET FUNCTION under a marketed 2'-MOE PS ASO - the row type NCATS asked for. Agonist ADP 1.8 uM; Born turbidimetric aggregometry on platelet-rich plasma, CHRONO-LOG 700 aggregometer, at week 36 of volanesorsen. Prespecified normality criterion (Methods 2.5): >=50% light transmission within 3 min indicates NO impairment of aggregation; 62% clears it. n=4 patients vs 4 matched healthy controls, no significant difference. Graded 0. Interpretive value: volanesorsen lowers the platelet COUNT by ~34% without impairing the FUNCTION of the platelets that remain - so count and function dissociate, and an in-vitro activation/aggregation assay is not a surrogate for the count endpoint.
